title: Home's other kinds of help on DCLab Code's card, memory in the chat, thinking always kept, and HyperAck after H3.1
request: Owner: did you update the chat UI; do not wait for me, keep going. Sync DCLab Code with R&D's new Home tracks (H7-H12), memory (35.x) and the thinking rule, then rerun HyperAck after H3.1.
spec: dclab-code docs/PARITY_PLAN.md; R&D H7-H12 routes under /api/drafts/{id}/(brief|answers|dashboard|prepared), /api/memory/proposals, the recall tool; R&D CLAUDE.md rule 8 (keep every model's thinking)
plan: draw each new Home turn kind on the card: answer (kpi, bars, line, with its numbers), prepared table, dashboard, decision brief, route suggestion, project answer
relay the person's clicks for them (answer edit and save, brief field, dashboard refresh, switch kind) through the person's channel, and the downloads through a checked GET relay
give the chat recall and the memory proposal route; keep corrections and reviews on DCLab's page
make thinking always kept (summarized); remove the setting that turned it off
lock R&D, run sync-check and the whole suite; rerun HyperAck

decisions.decision: thinking can no longer be turned off in DCLab Code; an old saved 'off' is dropped on load
decisions.why: the owner's rule: every model call keeps its thinking for training; a setting that loses it breaks the rule silently

decisions.decision: memory corrections and reviews are never relayed from the chat; only a proposal the person then confirms
decisions.why: memory changes what every agent reads later: the person decides it on DCLab's own page

decisions.decision: check H3.1 on the real table with no model when the live run was blocked by the account's credit
decisions.why: the deterministic path shows the question, the person's answer and the honest number at no cost; the live arm stays marked owed

decisions.decision: bars from zero, one hue per series from validated tokens (--chart-2, --chart-3), numbers in a table under the figure
decisions.why: a count compares by length; colour checked by the palette validator in light and dark; a table view for every chart

change: dclab-code ed3a146 (card kinds, relays, memory, thinking, sync-check fix, lock at R&D ecae6364), 867fc38 (parity plan).

findings.defect: sync-check crashed with a TypeError on the new per-answer routes
findings.scenario: npm run sync-check after adding answer_save and answer_edit acts whose path needs the answer's number
findings.cause: sync-check called each act's path(draft) with no args, so a.n was read from undefined
findings.fix: sync-check passes placeholder args ({n: '{n}'}) and lists the route with {n}
findings.test: npm run sync-check passes; the lock lists 86 person's writes

findings.defect: the whole suite hung for hours in tests/server.test.js
findings.scenario: npm test under heavy machine load (other sessions running): the keep-awake test failed at 300 ms and the file never exited
findings.cause: a timing-sensitive test under load; alone it passes in 0.6 s; not caused by this change
findings.fix: none to the code; the suite rerun with a stop timer passed 152/152

findings.defect: the live HyperAck rerun could not run
findings.scenario: hyper.py through DCLab Code on 4398: Claude's first reply was 'Credit balance is too low'
findings.cause: the Anthropic account had no credit
findings.fix: the owner adds credit; checked H3.1 on the rules path meanwhile

measurements.name: DCLab Code suite
measurements.gate: units, server, Chromium page tests all pass

measurements.name: HyperAck after H3.1, no model
measurements.gate: Home asks about deliverey_category_id before the build; the person's 'known' keeps it; the fares stay out; holdout read once near the research's 0.945
measurements.result: asked with the evidence (AUC 0.816); kept as a feature; fares out; holdout ROC-AUC 0.934 (0.923 to 0.946), CV 0.894, 2,219 rows; was 0.664

measurements.name: HyperAck live through the chat
measurements.gate: the same, with Claude and a recommend-only person

outcome: DCLab Code shows every kind of help R&D's Home gives and sends the person's clicks for each; the chat can recall memory and propose a preference; thinking is always kept. On the owner's HyperAck table the fixed Home asks about the strong column and, with the person's answer, the holdout is honest again (0.934).
lessons: When a sync tool reads a shape from code, give it placeholder arguments: a new route with a parameter should not crash the check.
When a live run is blocked, run the deterministic path on the same real data: it proves the rule, and the live arm stays honestly owed.
A setting that can turn off a training rule is a silent breach; remove it rather than default it.
risks: The live arm (reviewer names the moment, person says 'use your recommendation') is unit-tested but not live-checked.
The keep-awake server test is timing-sensitive under load.
The lock's onGitHub is false while other sessions have uncommitted dclab_core files.
